tasks.title: Give tools.Run and tools.RunArgv a runner-owned standard input and the ExecResult.IOErr field
steps: Write TS-04-1 to TS-04-5 in a new file tools/runner_stdin_test.go (package tools, so later seams are reachable); skip when ResolveShell fails or on windows; never edit tools/tools_test.go or tools/reqtool06_test.go (04-REQ-6.5). Confirm they fail to compile or fail

In tools/exec.go add `Stdin io.Reader` to ExecOptions (doc: nil means the null device, as REQ-TOOL-06; non-nil is copied through a pipe the runner owns and closed at io.EOF) and `IOErr error` to ExecResult (doc: a byte-moving failure that did not stop the process; Outcome is still classified from the exit status)
In runArgv keep `cmd.Stdin = nil` when opts.Stdin is nil

When opts.Stdin is non-nil, create a second os.Pipe (sr, sw) before cmd.Start and set cmd.Stdin = sr; on pipe failure close every fd already opened and return (ExecResult{}, err); after a successful Start close sr in the parent; on Start failure close sr, sw, pr and pw

Start a copier goroutine that loops: Read a chunk from opts.Stdin, Write it to sw. A Write error (EPIPE, os.ErrClosed) ends the copier quietly with no recorded error (04-REQ-1.3). io.EOF closes sw and ends. Any other read error is recorded under a mutex-guarded stdin state BEFORE sw is closed, then sw is closed and the copier ends; it never calls Read again after Read returned an error
Close sw through a sync.Once so the copier and the caller can both close it safely

After cmd.Wait and drainAfterExit, close sw (unblocking a copier stuck writing to a pipe a descendant still holds), read the recorded stdin error under the mutex and mark the state finished so a reader error arriving after the call returned is dropped without a data race; do not wait for the copier goroutine (04-REQ-1.5)

Set ExecResult.IOErr to fmt.Errorf("tools: reading stdin: %w", err) when a read error was recorded, so errors.Is(res.IOErr, readerErr) holds; leave Outcome/ExitCode classification from the wait status untouched
Update the Run and RunArgv doc comments to describe stdin
Run go test ./tools/ -run 'TS_04|Stdin' -race (where the toolchain supports -race) and confirm TS-04-5's goroutine count returns to baseline

tasks.title: Add KeepHead head truncation and the caller-named LogPath to the runner
steps: Write TS-04-6 to TS-04-14 and TS-04-16 in a new file tools/runner_output_test.go (package tools); TS-04-8 and TS-04-9 feed exact byte counts to ['cat'] through Stdin; TS-04-9 uses a fixed seed and at least 40 cases; TS-04-12 and the ro case of TS-04-13 skip on windows and as root

Add `KeepHead bool` (zero value keeps today's tail truncation; true keeps the first MaxBytes bytes) and `LogPath string` (complete output to a caller-chosen file, replacing SpillDir for that call, never deleted) to ExecOptions with doc comments
In runArgv choose the mode: TruncateTail unless opts.KeepHead, then TruncateHead; keep NewAccumulator(opts.MaxBytes, mode) so MaxBytes <= 0 still means DefaultByteLimit in both modes
Resolve LogPath: when relative, join it to opts.Dir, or to os.Getwd() when Dir is empty, then filepath.Abs the result so SpillPath is absolute

Before creating the output pipe and before cmd.Start: os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700) and os.OpenFile(path, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, 0o600); on either failure return (ExecResult{}, fmt.Errorf("tools: opening log %s: %w", path, err)) and start nothing (04-REQ-3.4)

In tools/accumulator.go add an unexported method (e.g. useFile(f *os.File, path string)) that installs a pre-opened file as the spill, so SpillPath reports the path from the start, including for empty output, and writeSpill never calls CreateTemp; when LogPath is set leave acc.SpillDir empty so no agentkit-exec-*.log is created (04-REQ-3.5)
If os.Pipe, the stdin pipe or cmd.Start fails after the log was opened, close the log handle and return the zero result and the error; leave the file in place
Keep Accumulator.Close as a handle close only and confirm no code path removes a LogPath file for any Outcome (04-REQ-3.7)
Confirm the head-mode and tail-mode markers come from Accumulator.marker unchanged, naming the spill or log path when one exists; do not change marker text
Update the Run/RunArgv doc comments ("tail truncation" becomes "tail truncation unless KeepHead") and run go test ./tools/

tasks.title: Report log and spill write failures and non-exit Wait errors in ExecResult.IOErr
steps: Write TS-04-15 and TS-04-27 in a new file tools/runner_ioerr_test.go (package tools); the /dev/full case of TS-04-15 runs on linux only; restore every seam with t.Cleanup

Add package-level test seams in tools/exec.go, identity in production: `var wrapExecFile = func(w io.Writer) io.Writer { return w }` applied to the Accumulator's spill/log file writer, and `var waitCmd = func(c *exec.Cmd) error { return c.Wait() }` used in place of cmd.Wait()

In tools/accumulator.go route writeSpill through an unexported io.Writer field (defaulting to the *os.File) that runArgv sets via wrapExecFile for both the LogPath file and the lazily created SpillDir file; keep the existing rule that the first error sets spillErr and stops further file writes while Write still returns len(p), nil so Output keeps accumulating
Add an unexported accessor (e.g. fileErr()) returning spillErr, which also covers a SpillDir MkdirAll/CreateTemp failure on first write

In runArgv, when waitErr is an *exec.ExitError keep today's exit-code and 128+signum logic; when waitErr is non-nil and not an ExitError record it as a Wait I/O error and derive exitCode and signaled from cmd.ProcessState (when non-nil) with the same signalExitCode rule, so Outcome is classified from the process state

Build ExecResult.IOErr with errors.Join of the stdin read error, the file write error wrapped as fmt.Errorf("tools: writing %s: %w", path, err), and the Wait I/O error, so errors.Is reaches each and IOErr is nil when none occurred
Read the file error only after drainSink.stop so no write races the read
Run TS-04-27's clean calls (exit 0, exit 3, Timeout, cancellation, Stdin round-trip, LogPath run) and confirm IOErr is nil on each; run go test ./tools/

tasks.title: Default ExecOptions.Env to ReducedEnv(nil) and pin the outcome and start-failure contract through RunArgv
steps: Write TS-04-17 to TS-04-19 in tools/runner_env_test.go and TS-04-20 to TS-04-26 in tools/runner_outcome_test.go (package tools); skip unix-only cases on windows; give TS-04-20 a fixed seed, at least 30 scenarios, through both RunArgv and Run, using t.Parallel subtests and short timings to bound runtime
Add an unexported helper effectiveEnv(env []string) []string returning ReducedEnv(nil) for a nil env and the slice verbatim otherwise (an empty non-nil slice stays empty)

In RunArgv compute the effective env before lookPathFor, pass it to lookPathFor so a bare name resolves through the child's PATH (04-REQ-4.3), and pass opts with Env set to it into runArgv; in Run do the same before runArgv
In runArgv always assign cmd.Env = opts.Env, so a non-nil empty slice gives the child an empty environment rather than the inherited one
Rewrite the ExecOptions.Env doc comment: nil means ReducedEnv(nil) (REQ-SEC-08, as tools.Options.Env); non-nil is used verbatim; pass os.Environ() for the full environment

Review the classification in runArgv: aborted = ctx.Err() != nil at the child's exit (so a caller deadline is abort), timedOut = !aborted && runCtx.Err() != nil, Duration taken before drainAfterExit, and the drain stopping on runCtx.Done without reclassifying; keep ClassifyOutcome's abort > timeout > signal > exit precedence
Confirm killGroup runs on both timeout and cancellation for the whole process group (proc_unix.go Setpgid, proc_windows.go taskkill /T) with no change to either file

Audit every return in Run, RunArgv and runArgv: only empty argv, ResolveShell/program-not-found, LogPath unopenable, pipe failure and cmd.Start failure (including a missing Dir) return a non-nil error, each with the zero ExecResult and every opened fd and log handle closed; every started call returns a nil error
Run go test ./tools/ and confirm the existing TestRunArgvResolvesTheProgramWithTheChildsPATH and TestGrandchildDoesNotSurviveTreeKill still pass unmodified

steps: Write TS-04-59 and TS-04-60 in a new tools/runner_smoke_test.go (package tools_test) against real sh, sleep and touch processes and the real filesystem, and TS-04-61 in a new root runner_metadata_smoke_test.go with an httptest.Server standing in for the Anthropic Messages API, the real execute tool, a real session store and NewAgentFromSession; confirm all three pass

Trace 04-PATH-1 through the code: RunArgv → effectiveEnv → lookPathFor(env) → runArgv → LogPath resolve/MkdirAll/OpenFile before Start → setProcessGroup → stdin copier → Accumulator in TruncateHead with the log file → ExecResult with SpillPath and nil IOErr; confirm each step calls the next and no stub remains

Search every file in the tasks' touches (tools/exec.go, tools/accumulator.go, tools/tools.go, tools/powershell.go, core/tool.go, core/message.go, batch.go, session/codec.go and the docs) for panic("not implemented"), TODO, FIXME, TBD and bare `return nil` on non-trivial paths, and remove any that remain
